headline: Residents testify on updated South Maui Community Plan

meeting.body: Maui County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee
meeting.summary: In South Maui, the committee heard public testimony on Bill 108, the updated South Maui Community Plan, and deferred the item.
meeting.recap: The only item was Bill 108 (2026), which would adopt an updated South Maui Community Plan.[[0:04:05]] The meeting was posted with no legislative action, so no vote was planned.[[0:04:26]] The committee met in South Maui to hear directly from residents.[[0:04:49]] The department said flooding is a major concern in South Maui.[[0:22:08]] One testifier said planned pumping of an aquifer would exceed its estimated sustainable yield.[[0:46:05]] One testifier asked the committee to go back to the CPAC version of the plan.[[0:55:00]] One testifier spoke in support of Bill 108.[[1:56:04]] One testifier asked for a two-to-three-year pause on building new homes while infrastructure is built.[[2:00:20]] The chair closed oral testimony, and written testimony remains open.[[2:12:34]] The chair said the committee has through October 8 to focus only on this plan.[[2:20:20]] The chair said the plan arrived August 4, giving the council one year.[[2:23:18]] The chair deferred the item.[[2:24:17]]
decided: The chair closed oral public testimony, and written testimony stays open for the whole process.
meeting.next: The committee will meet tomorrow morning in the council chambers with regular hybrid (in-person and online) procedures. The chair said the committee will start reviewing policies tomorrow. The chair said staff will upload a sheet listing which attachments to bring.

boards.name: Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

issues.oneLine: A testifier said planned pumping of an aquifer would exceed its estimated sustainable yield.
issues.why: The testifier said aquifers pumped too hard can be destroyed and do not recover.
issues.brief: A testifier said the central Maui water system's projected demand is already 98 percent of estimated capacity.[[#1]] A testifier said new developments plan to provide private water through reverse osmosis.[[#2]]
